judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble bundles an individual scientist and an institution into a single collective defined term "Recipient", so it is not clear whose acts bind whom, and the OCR-garbled definition parenthetical compounds the uncertainty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against the signature block (separate lines for "Recipient Scientist" and "Institution Official") and against paragraph 3's reference to "the Recipient's clinical facilities", the collective definition mostly holds together, though the dual-signatory structure hints the parties treated them as distinct.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Materials" is defined to include "progeny, portions, unmodified derivatives and any accompanying know-how or data" — "unmodified derivatives", "portions" and "progeny" are exactly the terms that carry more than one reasonable biological/legal meaning, and the closing reference to "altered forms of the Materials made by St. Jude" sits oddly with the exclusion of modified derivatives from the definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 3 expressly authorises the Recipient to produce a lentiviral vector clone "incorporating Materials", and paragraph 5 asserts St. Jude ownership of "the Materials and any progeny thereof", so whether the resulting modified construct is itself "Materials" is a live whole-instrument question this definition does not resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional compliance-with-laws undertaking whose "including, but not limited to" catch-all is expansive rather than restrictive, so the general-vs-specific tension is slight.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in paragraphs 1, 3, 7 or 8 pulls against sole responsibility for receipt, storage, handling and use; the indemnity in paragraph 7 runs in the same direction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Sole purpose", "quantities sufficient to complete a Phase I clinical trial", "provided to a commercial entity" and "research that is subject to consulting or licensing obligations to another party" are all boundary terms a court would have to fix, and the carve-out for U.S. government grantee obligations is an expressio unius invitation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits directly against paragraph 5, which contemplates that the Recipient may file a patent application or "commercialize a product" derived from the Materials — a use paragraph 3's prohibition on commercial-entity involvement and licensing-encumbered research appears to forbid.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short obligation to furnish a copy of any publication and acknowledge the source; the only softness is "experimental results obtained from the use of the Materials", plus severe OCR corruption in the middle of the sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 5 imposes a separate pre-submission 30-day review right, and this clause speaks only of providing a copy after publication, leaving a mild overlap rather than a genuine conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Recipient agrees to contact St. Jude to determine ownership interests, if any" states no substantive rule, and the following sentence ("Ownership shall [follow] inventorship according to US patent law") contradicts the opening acknowledgment of St. Jude's ownership of Materials and progeny; "could not have been produced but for the use of the Materials" is an open-ended reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Against paragraph 1 (no express or implied licenses granted) and paragraph 3 (no commercialisation or commercial-entity involvement without consent), this clause's assumption that the Recipient may patent and commercialise derived products is difficult to harmonise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard all-caps warranty disclaimer and consequential-damages exclusion; its terms are definite, and the only defects are OCR artefacts rather than drafting ones.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is misnumbered as a second "5", and paragraph 10 provides that "Sections 5, 5 and 7 shall survive", so which paragraph 5 survives — and whether this one does — is genuinely uncertain from the instrument as a whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The indemnity is broad and one-sided ("claims ... of any nature whatsoever", "arising out of or related to") and contains no carve-out for St. Jude's own negligence, which is the usual point of construction in such clauses.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with paragraph 2 (sole responsibility), the warranty disclaimer, and paragraph 10's survival list, which expressly names section 7.
